response.query: How can process tracing and timeline-comparison methods be structured to causally link discrete archival discoveries to later narrative re-authoring and changes in meaning?
response.answer: Process tracing links archival discoveries to later changes by following evidence trails; timeline-comparison methods align these findings with shifts in narrative and meaning. This causal linkage helps understand how historical events influence contemporary interpretations.

results.title: Design Research and Object-Oriented Ontology - De Gruyter
results.content: For example, in the case of the Polly project OOO was initially used generativity to develop design concepts; for the Tarot of Things project, the cards facilitate a performative exploration of OOO; with the Living Room of the Future project a functional prototype becomes an analogy for OOO itself, which then becomes a conceptual framework to articulate attributes of the design that are not immediately obvious from the surface. Whilst the LRoTF is a rich example of Design Research in an IoT context, and as such there seems to be a sensible fit for applying the lens of More-Than Human Centred Design either in a generative or analytic idiom, this paper is about OOO, so, to that end, what’s the new contribution here? Both the Internet of Things Game and our deck of IoT Tarot cards demonstrate how OOO’s inherent interest in all types of ‘otherness’ can simultaneously be generative and analytical—helping to develop novel methods to practice More-Than Human design, each which in their own means of focusing unique perspectives.
